title: Security guards and layered defense-in-depth
goal_html: Groups act as physical security consultants reviewing layer proposals for a fictional facility, Novara Data Center, and decide whether each proposed layer set is STRONG, ADEQUATE, or WEAK, and what single addition would most improve a weak configuration. Ties to LO 2.3.B (security guards and layered defense-in-depth) and the course skill Mitigate Risk.
reference_html:
Layer sheet (print or project)

# Facility Layers present Categories Rating What's missing
1 Novara-Annex lobby guard, roving night patrol ? ? ?
2 Novara-Branch perimeter fence, badge reader, CCTV ? ? ?
3 Novara-Warehouse unlocked side door only ? ? ?
4 Novara-Lab 3 separate CCTV feeds ? ? ?
5 Novara-Core fence, guard post, badge reader, mantrap, CCTV ? ? ?
steps_html:
1. (5 min) Each group reads rows 1-2 and individually lists the distinct control categories present for each (perimeter, personnel, electronic, barrier, monitoring).
  2. (5 min) Group discusses: row 1 has two layers but why does that not raise the depth score above 1? Reach consensus on the "categories," "rating," and "what's missing" columns for rows 1-2.
  3. (5 min) Repeat for rows 3-4, paying special attention to why three CCTV feeds (row 4) still count as only one category, and why row 3 has a depth score of zero rather than one.
  4. (5 min) For row 5, the group must decide whether this facility is STRONG or ADEQUATE, and justify the answer by counting distinct categories, not layers.
  5. (5 min) Each group opens the simulation and checks their ratings against the sim's scoring for the analogous facilities; groups revise any incorrect calls and note which category was missing in each WEAK or ADEQUATE case.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one member is the "facility manager" (proposes which single new layer would most cheaply raise the depth score), one is the "budget owner" (must justify that the proposed layer's cost is worth the new category it closes, not a redundant one), and remaining members are "auditors" (challenge whether a proposed addition actually introduces a new category or just duplicates an existing one, e.g., a second guard vs. a badge reader). For row 1 (Novara-Annex), the group must specifically debate whether adding a third guard or adding a badge reader is the better use of budget, and explain why in terms of depth score.
exit_html: Each student writes one sentence: "Facility X is rated [STRONG/ADEQUATE/WEAK] because it has [N] distinct control categories, and adding a [category] layer such as [example] would most improve its posture."
